gloss_distractors: popular with a very young audience
senses.definition: Staying useful and relevant for a long time without needing to be updated.
senses.caution: Most often said of content such as articles or training. Few things are truly evergreen, so use it only when the topic is not tied to a date.
senses.example: Write evergreen guides instead of news posts, so they still bring in readers next year.

cues.text: You plan a content calendar and want articles that will still bring in readers two years from now, unlike a post about this week's product launch. What marketing word, borrowed from a tree that keeps its leaves, describes that content?
A training deck on how to give feedback is still useful five years later, and a colleague describes it with a word borrowed from trees that never lose their leaves.
A friend says a classic song never goes out of date, and you use the adjective borrowed from trees that stay green all year.

distractors: Full of new ideas, especially ones that nobody has tried before.
Done in small steps over a long period of time.
Made for one customer rather than for the general public, with features chosen only for them.
Easy to replace while the rest of the system keeps working without anyone noticing.
Lasting only a short time, and meant to.
